A country of unspoilt nature, history and heritage, rich in stories told within the walls of its cities, Poland is simply a destination you should not miss. On your travels you may have tried famous European countries such as Switzerland, Italy and France, but we invite you to visit Poland for a beautiful European flavour that is unique in character and different from anything you have encountered before. You can learn a great deal about the events of World War II, wander the Polish countryside, or climb mountains and ski in winter. Do not miss the delicious dishes of Poland’s distinctive cuisine. You can visit more than one city and discover Poland’s heritage, culture and architecture, as well as enjoying the beauty and magic of its nature. Poland enjoys a strategic location in th: Poland enjoys a strategic location in the heart of Europe and is considered a bridge between East and West. It is bordered by Germany to the west, the Czech Republic and Slovakia to the south, Ukraine and Belarus to the east, Lithuania and the Russian Kaliningrad region to the north-east, and the Baltic Sea to the north.
Which made it throughout history an area: This has made it, throughout history, an area of conflict and influence between the major European powers. Its terrain is varied, including the northern plains that stretch towards the Baltic Sea and the highlands and mountains of the south, such as the Sudetes and the Carpathians.
If you are one of the travelers who pref: If you are a traveller who likes to visit more than one country, Poland’s location makes it easy to combine your trip with visits to neighbouring European countries. You will find that some of these countries can be reached by car with no need to fly, which may make your trip more economical.
Poland's culture is one of the attractio: Poland’s culture: one of the attractions of tourism in Poland
Poland has a rich and diverse cultural h: Poland has a rich and diverse cultural heritage that reflects its long and complex history. It has been the cradle of many prominent figures in literature, music and science, such as the composer Frédéric Chopin and the Nobel Prize-winning scientist Marie Curie.
Poland is famous for its classical music: Poland is famous for its classical music and cultural festivals, with many events worth attending. These include the Krakow Film Festival and the Krakow Music Festival, both of which attract large numbers of visitors every year, as well as the Woodstock Poland Festival, which you can attend for free to enjoy a variety of musical performances. For lovers of modern music, the Warsaw Festival is the perfect choice, as is the Orange Warsaw Festival. Learn about beliefs and religions before: Beliefs and religions to know about before travelling to Poland
More than 90% of the population professe: More than 90% of the population is Christian, and the vast majority are Catholic. Religion plays an important role in Polish daily life and culture. The Catholic Church has been, and remains, highly influential in Polish society, especially during periods of political unrest.
Holidays and traditions that you can obs: Holidays and traditions you can observe while travelling in Poland
Poland is famous for its rich traditions: Poland is famous for its rich traditions, especially at religious festivals such as Christmas (Wigilia) and Easter (Wielkanoc). It also has many cultural and artistic festivals that reflect its cultural diversity, as we mentioned.
One of the Polish customs is that you pa: One Polish custom is to pay the exact amount for your purchases, otherwise you may run into difficulty. Always keep change with you when shopping and buying food. When eating with others, it is important to say “thank you”, even if those who prepared the food are not present. Saying “thank you” after a meal is their way of expressing gratitude and is considered good manners; by contrast, it is considered rude to eat and then leave in silence. Expect strangers to ask to share your table if no other tables are free.
The Polish citizen is very punctual, whe: Poles are very punctual, whether for official occasions or meetings. If you visit a Polish home, you should bring sweets, flowers or a souvenir from your country. Shake hands with your hosts on entering. Some will ask you to take off your shoes and offer you slippers, while others do not mind, as it has become a rather old-fashioned custom. The host will often prepare a large meal for you. Let the host know that you cannot eat pork or lard or drink alcohol because of your religious beliefs. Poles respect other beliefs and will never force you to do any of this.
If you are a smoker, avoid smoking at ho: If you are a smoker, avoid smoking indoors. Polish smokers smoke outside the house or by the window. Try to avoid steering the conversation towards politics or controversial topics. If you are Muslim and the host family is Christian, expect some questions about Islam; the host’s curiosity is quite normal. Conversation usually begins once the meal is over, so never leave straight after eating. You will notice that the farewell is warmer than the welcome, as the host has now got to know you better.
History of Poland The main attraction of: The history of Poland: a main attraction of tourism in Poland
Poland's history is full of major events: Poland’s history is full of major events, from the medieval age of prosperity, when Poland was one of Europe’s largest countries, to the partitions that led to its disappearance from the map of Europe in the 18th century and its re-emergence as an independent country after World War I. During World War II, Poland was one of the worst-affected countries: it was invaded by Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union and lost millions of its people.
Poland's history is rich in events and h: Poland’s history is rich in events and heroic stories of the struggle to regain its land, throw off occupation and win back its independence, which is one of Poland’s defining traits. Poland went through the horrors of World War I and World War II and the harsh grip of communism, but each time it regained its strength and rebuilt itself.

Polish cuisine is very diverse, which is: Polish cuisine is very varied, which is one of Poland’s attractions. Among the most famous Polish dishes are pierogi (dumplings filled with cheese, potatoes, meat or fruit), gołąbki (cabbage stuffed with minced meat and rice and cooked in tomato sauce), kiełbasa (garlic-flavoured sausages) and bigos (known as hunter’s stew).
As for halal food, it is easy to obtain: As for halal food, it is easy to find in Krakow and Warsaw, where there are many Indian, Turkish and Arab restaurants serving halal food. Some Polish restaurants also serve halal food; just check for a halal certificate before ordering. Many Polish dishes are also vegetarian, prepared with potatoes, dough, vegetables, mushrooms and cheese.

The weather varies in Poland and it has: The weather in Poland varies, with 4 seasons as follows:
The winter season is from December until: Winter runs from December to February and brings cold weather and snowfall, with temperatures sometimes below zero. Winter is therefore the best time for lovers of winter sports such as skiing.
Spring is from March to May and enjoys s: Spring runs from March to May and brings somewhat milder weather than winter. Temperatures range between 5 and 15 degrees, with rain on some days and sunshine on others.
Summer is between the months of June and: Summer runs from June to August. It is a warm season compared with winter and spring, with temperatures reaching twenty-five degrees.
The fall semester is between September a: Autumn runs from September to November. The weather falls into two phases: it starts warm and then turns cold, and snow even falls in some areas in November. Autumn is known for its dazzling colours, and the leaves begin to fall.
It depends on your personal preferences. Many visitors prefer spring and autumn for their mild weather, especially as those months offer better prices and fewer tourists, so sightseeing is less crowded. Others prefer winter, to enjoy winter sports and the market decorations in the run-up to Christmas and the festive activities.
